transcript.answer: The web UI uses one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws` (the URL is set by `LORE_WS_URL`, formerly `LORE_PLANS_WS_URL`). It carries JSON text frames with client-chosen channel ids and multiplexes named channels. The `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript. It is authorized by a token minted through POST /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream-token. The `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's Hocuspocus collaboration bytes to the same collaboration server, and the collab-token handshake stays inside the tunnel. The web-ui keeps the socket in a provider above every page, so navigating from a plan to its run keeps the connection. This replaced the earlier SSE stream (ADR-037) under ADR-048 (PR #2122). The row-id cursor, the catch-up-then-live semantics and the Postgres NOTIFY fan-out are unchanged. On the server, there is one feed per run.

judgements.reason: The answer covers the essentials: one WebSocket per browser tab at lore-api's /api/ws, multiplexed JSON channels including run and plan, and replacement of the earlier SSE stream. It omits the runs channel but contradicts nothing.
